name: Aisi
world_status: accessible description is silent on stress

earlier_scan.source_named: Daniels, Don. 2015. A Reconstruction of Proto-Sogeram. PhD dissertation, UC Santa Barbara (contains synchronic Aisi phonology sketch); eScholarship blocked automated access

sources.citation: Daniels, Don. 2016. Magɨ: An Undocumented Language of Papua New Guinea. Oceanic Linguistics 55(1): 199-224. doi:10.1353/ol.2016.0004. Sec. 3.1 Phonology pp. 205-206 (Aisi phoneme inventory Table 3). ANU Open Research hdl:1885/108658.
sources.note: Nothing: segmental inventories and allophony of Magɨ vs Aisi only; 'stress' and 'accent' occur only in non-technical senses.

sources.citation: Daniels, Don Roger. 2015. A Reconstruction of Proto-Sogeram: Phonology, Lexicon, and Morphosyntax. PhD dissertation, University of California, Santa Barbara. 1127 pp. Appendix 4 'Aisi Grammar Sketch' pp. 766-882; phonology sec. 4.2 pp. 771-776 (4.2.1 Morphophonemics pp. 775-776); Aisi historical sections 2.4.2-2.4.4 pp. 101-108. eScholarship ark:/13030/qt1kj4174g.
sources.note: Nothing for Aisi. Sec. 4.2 (pp. 771-776) covers consonant/vowel inventories, /b d g/ lenition to [β ɾ ɣ] non-initially, status of /r/, diphthongs /ai/ and /ou/~/au/, glide vs vowel syllabification, minimal pairs for /ɨ/, and morphophonemics (ɨ-epenthesis, rounding, nasal assimilation); no word on stress, accent, tone or syllable weight. The only stress remarks in the whole dissertation are p. 71 (Mand section): 'Further research into the stress systems of the Sogeram languages might reveal a consistent pattern.' and p. 338 (West Sogeram final *a loss 'regular for commonly stressed word classe…

sources.citation: Z'graggen, John A. 1980. A comparative word list of the Southern Adelbert Range languages, Madang Province, Papua New Guinea. Pacific Linguistics D-33. Canberra: ANU. Musak = H4; 315-item list + pronoun paradigms p. 83.
sources.note: Nothing: semi-phonemic transcription without stress marks; introduction has no prosodic remark about Musak (only Isabi and Biyom noted as tonal).

sources.citation: Z'graggen, J. A. 1971. Classificatory and typological studies in languages of the Madang District. Pacific Linguistics C-19. Canberra: ANU. Musak 44/Mu sec. 2.22.42.12 p. 62; Emuan Family typology sec. 2.22.42.3 pp. 62-63; Adelbert Range Phylum typology sec. 2.22.8 p. 74.
sources.note: No stress statement. p. 74 sec. 2.22.8 item 2, for the whole Adelbert Range Phylum (which includes Musak): 'None of the languages appears to be tonal.' Emuan typology p. 63 lists segmental traits only (glottal stop and voiced/voiceless stop contrast 'only in Musak', no r/l differentiation).
